top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B038) is the best-bounded and most mature discovery on the slate. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work on exporting versus foreign investment moved trade analysis from industries to firms. This gave a selection and reallocation channel for the gains from trade. Firm-level facts such as exporter premia were documented before the model. The model's contribution is the mechanism and its testable implications, which have been examined on customs and production microdata for over twenty years. The credit set is two names and closely tracks the discovery. I read firm selection as a distinct step from the 2008 prize on scale economies and location. The citation should name the mechanism and not any welfare magnitude, since the magnitudes depend on elasticity assumptions. The main residual weakness is that Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum are outside the credited names. A narrow citation reduces that concern but does not remove it. P002 (B015) ranks second because it is mature and very influential, but its three-name attribution is contestable and survival of the framework does not confirm the specific credited building blocks. P004 (B050) has clean attribution but thinner direct identification of the collateral channel and some overlap with the 2022 prize. P003 (B036) has strong local-labour-market identification, but its discovery boundary and Dorn-versus-Katz credit remain unsettled. P000 ranks last because several candidates are mature, substantive and defensible. Support counts were not used as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. My profile shows no co-authorship or institutional tie to Melitz, Helpman, Redding, or the credited names on P002, P003 or P004. I disclose that Tommy Andersson is a Lund colleague and also prefers B038, and I treat his view as non-independent. My economic-history preference for new measurement tested on microdata may bias me toward B038. No ties are adjudicated.
